reason: The text explicitly presents Yahweh's goal to help the Hebrew people through the divinely-appointed judge Samson. The angel announces that the unborn child 'will begin to save (הִשׁוּעַ) Israel from the hand of the Philistines' (Judges 13:5). Throughout the narrative, Yahweh actively empowers Samson through His Spirit (רוּחַ יְהוָה) to defeat the Philistines through multiple acts of deliverance—slaying 30 Philistines in Ashkelon, burning their crops via 300 foxes, killing 1,000 warriors with a donkey's jawbone, and finally destroying the Philistine leadership by collapsing their temple. Samson himself acknowledges God's salvific purpose: 'You have given your servant this great deliverance' (15:18). God responds to Samson's prayers for assistance (water in 15:19, strength in 16:28), and Samson is explicitly designated as one who 'judged Israel twenty years' (15:20; 16:31). The narrative structure consistently demonstrates Yahweh's active intervention on behalf of Israel against their oppressors.
